name: AL-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+33 partisan lean in a deep-red Alabama district
Aderholt is a long-tenured incumbent with a large financial edge
Democratic challenger raised only ~$16k with negligible cash on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~99%
model.rationale: The district's R+33 lean, Aderholt's incumbency, and his roughly 65-to-1 fundraising advantage over Amanda Pusczek leave the Democrat no realistic path, and markets price a Republican win near certainty. The forecast stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Nothing realistically changes this; only an unforeseen incumbent scandal or withdrawal would matter.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Alabama's 4th District is among the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+33. Robert Aderholt has held the seat since 1997 and is running again with about $750,000 on hand after raising over $1 million. His Democratic opponent, Amanda Pusczek, has raised under $16,000 and reports only a few hundred dollars in cash.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 99 percent. With no competitive spending and a challenger lacking resources, the seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands.
